pr.title: simplifycfg: Mark as changed when start is modified in collapse goto chain
pr.author: dianqk

analysis.summary: SimplifyCfg's goto-chain collapsing could rewrite a block's start target without setting the pass's `changed` flag. The fix records whether the start actually moved before assigning the collapsed destination, so callers/fixpoint machinery observe the modification.
analysis.trigger: Collapsing a chain of single-target `Goto` terminators whose head is the `start` basic block, when the final destination differs from that original `start`.
preconditions: The CFG contains a goto chain followed to its final target (`current = target` in the collapse loop).
The rewritten `start` value is not already equal to the chain's final block (`*start != last`).
The caller relies on the `changed` flag to decide whether MIR was modified or whether another simplification iteration is needed.
analysis.originalLogic: The simplifier walks a goto chain to compute `let last = current;`, then performs `*start = last;`, and continues processing the saved terminators (`while let Some((current, mut terminator)) = terminators.pop()`).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: It replaced `*start` with the collapsed chain destination but did not set `*changed`, so an actually modified start block was reported as unchanged. The correction adds `*changed |= *start != last;` immediately before `*start = last;`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR control-flow graphs processed by `CfgSimplifier` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/simplify.rs`, specifically blocks whose terminator is a `TerminatorKind::Goto { target }` and whose start block is being collapsed along a goto chain.
pitfalls: Mutating the `start` block is a separate observable change from mutating the saved terminator targets; the `changed` flag must cover both.
Set `changed` only on a real difference (`*start != last`), not unconditionally, to preserve accurate change reporting.
Updating `*start` without marking change can leave callers/fixpoint iteration believing the CFG is unchanged and stopping before reaching a stable form.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused MIR/unit regression around `CfgSimplifier::collapse_goto_chain`: construct two inputs differing only in the start-chain shape—one where the start already equals the final goto destination and one where it points to an intermediate goto—then assert the resulting start value and the `changed` flag (false in the first case, true in the second). The supplied patch itself contains only the compiler change, so no specific test file or expectation can be cited.
